reports.title: Ambarella, Inc. Announces Third Quarter Fiscal Year 2027 Financial Results

desk.headline: Revenue up 6.2% to $115.2m, below estimates; Q4 revenue guide of $70–75m far below consensus as memory shortage hits customers
results: Revenue rose 6.2% to $115.2m, short of the $119.8m estimate and at the low end of the company's own range, as consumer IoT sales disappointed.
Edge AI revenue reached a record, but non-GAAP gross margin slipped to 59.5% from 60.9%.
Non-GAAP EPS was $0.28 (vs $0.27); the GAAP loss narrowed to $0.29 a share as R&D spending fell 5%.
Cash and marketable securities rose to $282.8m from $272.3m a quarter earlier.

guidance.summary: Q4 revenue is guided to only $70–75m, a steep drop from $115.2m and well below the roughly $112.6m analysts expected, because soaring memory prices and shortages are making customers cut orders. Non-GAAP gross margin of 59.0–60.25% and opex of $57.5–59.5m are expected.

points: CEO Fermi Wang said memory pricing and availability began to have a material impact, with customers saving scarce memory for their newest products.
Consumer IoT fell short and declined from Q2; automotive was close to plan but one customer's supplier could not get enough memory.
Most of the lost revenue is orders pushed out rather than cancelled, and management assumes memory conditions stay this tight through fiscal 2028.
Wang still expects fiscal 2028 to be a growth year, driven mainly by new chips such as CV7 and CV8 ramping in the second half.
Discretionary spending is under review, but R&D investment will continue; receivable days rose to 47 from 32.
call.source: Call coverage: Investing.com transcript, 24 Nov 2026; Stocktwits, 24 Nov 2026

watch: Whether memory supply and prices ease, and how many pushed-out orders come back.
Ramp of the new CV7 and CV8 chips behind the fiscal 2028 growth claim.
Any cost cuts given the much lower revenue run-rate.
